extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners and attorneys subject to USPTO discipline; OED staff and respondents in USPTO disciplinary proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Final Order resolving a USPTO disciplinary complaint by settlement; sets forth stipulated facts, legal conclusions, and agreed sanctions under USPTO disciplinary regulations and cites applicable state professional conduct violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of USPTO Disciplinary Rules (37 C.F.R. § 10.20 & related)
rubrics_metrics.description: At all times relevant hereto, Respondent has been registered as an agent to practice before the United States Patent and Trademark Office ("USPTO or "the Office") and is subject to the Disciplinary Rules of the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility set forth at 37 C.F.R. § 10.20 & m. Respondent's registration number is 48,536.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Being a registered practitioner before the USPTO makes one subject to the USPTO disciplinary rules; registration details (e.g., registration number) are part of the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: State professional conduct violations as grounds for USPTO discipline (Virginia Rules 1.1, 1.3(a), 1.4(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent violated Virginia Rules of Professional Conduct 1.1, 1.3(a), and 1.4(a) in connection with representation in multiple matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Violations of a jurisdiction's Rules of Professional Conduct (here, Virginia RPC 1.1—competence; 1.3(a)—diligence; 1.4(a)—communication) are substantive grounds that can support USPTO discipline where the respondent is disciplined on ethical grounds by that jurisdiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct examples constituting violations (failure to file/communicate/furnish records)
rubrics_metrics.description: Factual examples include: failing to file a Petition for Appeal and failing to communicate that the case had been dismissed; failing to file a required affidavit when seeking withdrawal of an appeal and failing to inform client of dismissal; failing to file required transcript or statement of facts and failing to respond to an Order to Show Cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific failures in appellate practice (not filing required appellate documents, not communicating with clients, not responding to court orders) illustrate how competence, diligence, and communication rules may be breached and lead to discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal/related USPTO rule: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) via § 10.23(c)(5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Based on the information contained in paragraphs 1 through 9, Respondent acknowledges that his conduct violated 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) via 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(c)(5) by being disciplined on ethical grounds by the Commonwealth of Virginia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO may take disciplinary action where a practitioner has been disciplined by a state bar for ethical violations; acknowledgement of such a violation is a basis for USPTO sanction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement agreement requirements (37 C.F.R. § 11.26)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and Respondent's proposed settlement agreement sets forth certain stipulated facts, legal conclusions, and sanctions to which the OED Director and Respondent have agreed in order to resolve voluntarily a disciplinary complaint against Respondent. The proposed settlement agreement, which satisfies the requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 11.26, resolves all disciplinary action by the United States Patent and Trademark Office arising from the stipulated facts set forth below.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A settlement agreement submitted to the USPTO Director must meet the § 11.26 requirements (i.e., include stipulated facts, legal conclusions, agreed sanctions) and, if approved, resolves the disciplinary matters covered by those stipulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorized sanctions and remedies (public reprimand; publication)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent be, and hereby is, publicly reprimanded; The OED Director shall publish this Final Order; The OED Director shall publish the following Notice in the Official Gazette: Notice of Reprimand ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sanctions available/ordered under the cited statutory/regulatory authority include public reprimand and mandatory publication of the reprimand in USPTO channels (Final Order, Official Gazette). The text of the Notice summarizes the basis for discipline and the rules violated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice obligations under 37 C.F.R. § 11.59
rubrics_metrics.description: In accordance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.59, the OED Director shall give notice of public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the State where the practitioner is admitted to practice, to courts where the practitioner is known to be admitted, and the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When discipline is imposed, the OED Director must notify relevant state disciplinary bodies, courts where the practitioner is admitted, and make the information public as prescribed by § 11.59.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory authority for USPTO disciplinary action (35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.26, 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: This action is taken pursuant to the provisions of 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.26 and 11.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary proceedings and sanctions before the USPTO are grounded in statutory (35 U.S.C. § 32) and regulatory (37 C.F.R.) authority; settlement terms and publication/notice obligations derive from those provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of costs in settlement
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and Respondent shall each bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of this agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A settlement may specify who bears costs; here, each party bears its own costs—demonstrating that cost allocation is an express, negotiable element of disciplinary settlements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent acknowledgement and consent to discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent agreed and it is hereby Ordered that: [sanctions]. Based on the information, Respondent acknowledges that his conduct violated the cited regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlement-style dispositions require respondent acknowledgement of violations and consent to the agreed sanctions; such admission is part of the record and grounds for entry of the Final Order.
